title: Q2 Dedicated: Anticipatory Warm-Pool Scheduling & SLA Fallback Matrix
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: As committed customers increase reserved capacity usage, we need a predictable, auditable scheduling system that proactively warms reserved GPU pools for anticipated surges while guaranteeing a clear, tested fallback path that preserves SLAs when warm capacity is exhausted. This ticket defines the Q2 plan to design, pilot, and publish an operational schedule and fallback matrix for anticipatory warm-pools across Dedicated clusters.

Scope: Plan, implement controls, and run a 6-week pilot with one enterprise beta customer and two internal traffic classes. Inputs include demand signal sources (forecast, historical usage, customer schedule), constraints (budgeted reserved hours, burst budgets), and operator approval windows. Outcome is a documented schedule, CLI + Console controls prototype, and a verified rollback/fallback matrix integrated with the routing layer.

Out of scope: Full autoscaler redesign, pricing model rewrite, and multi-region warm-pool federation (will be follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Eng, SRE, and Sales Engineering
Pilot warms pools per schedule for >90% of target surge windows without manual intervention
Fallback matrix triggers degraded-mode routing (fallthrough to burst or alternate region) within SLO thresholds in <=30s
Console control shows schedule and last-run audit trail; CLI exposes enable/disable and manual override
Post-pilot cost delta report comparing warm vs cold scenarios and recommended guardrails
decisions: Use three signals for anticipatory warming: 7-day rolling forecast, committed-customer calendar, and short-term traffic spike detector
Pilot will use fractionally reserved warm-pools (30% of reserved capacity) to limit cost exposure
Fallback policy: prefer degraded model variant routing (smaller context or quantized variant) before cross-region failover to minimize data egress
tradeoffs: Aggressive warming reduces cold-start latency but increases committed-hour consumption and cost
Conservative warming saves budget but risks SLA blips during unpredicted spikes
Local fallback keeps data locality but may exhaust local burst pools faster than regional failover
